newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Slow Australian stocks pare gains by close.
newsitem.headline: Slow Australian stocks pare gains by close.

text.p: Australian shares closed just firmer on Thursday, the market sliding off its highs in the afternoon as bellwether BHP faded amid heavy options trade as the January series options reached expiry.
The All Ordinaries index added 3.5 points to 2,417.7.
The leaders turned in a mixed performance with brokers saying much of the activity was related to options positions rather than fresh corporate leads.
"Lots of the activity was because of the options," said a Sydney-based dealer, noting that the leaders were nearly always subject to choppy trade ahead of options expiries.
"There was a reasonable tone about it but they were always going to be moved about today."

Corporate news in the leaders was light but at the smaller end shares in biotech company Progen rocketed 20 percent to close at A$0.92 (US$0.71) after it reported encouraging results from tests of its anti-cancer compound. Progen said the PI-88 compound inhibited the growth rate of human colon cancer in mice which had been transplanted with primary human tumours.
Gawler Craton gold hopeful Desertstone failed to fare as well. Its shares fell 47 percent to A$0.34 after its progress report on the Lake Torrens project failed to meet expectations.
In the second line banks, Bank of Melbourne shares soared nearly four percent to A$8.91 as takeover speculation stirred again ahead of the Wallis inquiry conclusion in March.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to seven, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
